In every settled rollout, PF1 was properly revealed by A2 and cited in justification_fact_ids, so neither NEVER REVEALED nor TELEPATHY applies. The failure is that the settlement's commitments never include a direct carrier-contact or coordination-line commitment targeting Lt. Morgan. In rollout 1, the commitments list a 'carrier_appointment' entry for Lt. Morgan but it only records the appointment details — it does not commit to contacting the carrier or a coordination line. In rollout 2, the commitments include only a 'board_entry' for Lt. Morgan to enter the appointment, with no carrier-contact commitment at all. In rollout 3, the commitments include a 'movement_board_entry' for Lt. Morgan and an 'inspection_log_transmission' for SFC Patel, but again no carrier-contact or coordination-line commitment targeting Lt. Morgan. This is consistent across all three: the group had PF1 (including the 1000 hold-until limit), cited it, set carrier_coordination_required=true in rollouts 1 and 3 (false in rollout 2), but never produced the specific commitment type the check requires. This is an ENCODING MISMATCH: the check expects a commitment of type 'carrier_contact' or 'carrier_coordination' (or equivalent) targeting Lt. Morgan, but the model naturally produces a 'carrier_appointment' or 'board_entry' commitment instead — it records the appointment fact rather than committing to a direct carrier-contact action. The PF1 'why' field states the requirement for 'a direct carrier-contact or coordination-line commitment targeting Lt. Morgan,' but nothing in the shared_context or the transcript prompts the agents to create that specific commitment type; the model treats entering the appointment on the board as the fulfillment. C6 failed in rollout 2 only (tally 2/3). In rollout 2, carrier_coordination_required was set to false even though PF1 (including the 1000 hold-until limit) was revealed and cited. This is MISAPPLIED: the group had the correct information — the carrier's 1000 hold-until limit was explicitly stated in the PF1 reveal — but the settlement set carrier_coordination_required to false, directly contradicting what PF1 implies. The same implication was correctly applied in rollouts 1 and 3 (both set it to true), so the fact's wording is not inherently ambiguous; rather, the model in rollout 2 failed to derive the coordination requirement from the hold-until limit. Rollout 0 auto-failed on the turn cap at 12 turns without settling. Both PF1 and PF2 were revealed by turn 9, and all substantive information was on the table by turn 8. The conversation continued through turns 10-11 with A1 asking for a spotter assignment and A3 saying he had no available soldier, but no settle occurred. This is a STRUCTURAL problem, not a pacing problem: the settle-eligibility condition appears to require a completed spotter_assignment commitment (a specific named individual confirmed to SFC Patel), but the scenario gives no agent a roster or authority to name a spotter — A1 explicitly says he has no personnel visibility, and A3 says he has no available soldier from the motor pool. The group is stuck in a loop where the publication checklist requires a named spotter but no agent can produce one, so the settle condition never triggers. Raising turn_cap alone would not fix this because the agents would continue the same impasse indefinitely.
